summary_1line: Bhishma recounts a debate on whether kings should execute criminals, weighing compassion, social order, and alternative punishments.

image_candidates.scene_text: Prince Satyavat stands before his father Dyumatsena, arguing passionately that killing criminals cannot truly be righteous.
A king sits in judgment while bound robbers are brought before him, as priests and counselors debate whether to execute or spare them.
A repentant offender kneels before a Brahmana and the king, swearing never again to commit sin while chains lie at his feet.
